notify_user.desc: Send a non-blocking fire-and-forget notification. Use for progress updates like "Starting analysis…" or "Build complete." — never blocks. For questions that need an answer, use ask_user instead.

params.title: Notification title. Default: "AI Assistant"
params.duration_seconds: How long the toast stays visible (Windows/Linux only). Default: 5 s.

ask_user.desc: Ask the user a short question via a browser dialog. Opens the dialog immediately and returns a token — call get_user_response(token=…) to retrieve the answer. Use ONLY for discovery questions that require a user decision or clarification — NOT for writing solutions, explanations, or progress updates. Long answers, code, and summaries belong in your terminal/chat response, not in this dialog. Keep the question concise. If your environment has other tools also named ask_user, use this one (bmcptools).

params.question: A short, focused question. Do NOT include long reasoning, solutions, or explanations here — write those in your response text instead. Ask one clear question only.
params.details: Optional supplementary context rendered as markdown below the question. Use this for things the user needs to see alongside the question — e.g. a summary of what you just changed, your current findings, or relevant background. Keep the question itself short; put the substance here.
params.title: Dialog window title. Default: "AI Assistant"
params.subtitle: Subtitle shown below the title (e.g. your agent name).
params.choices: Optional quick-reply chips. User can tap a chip and/or type a custom reply.
params.allow_freeform: Allow freeform text input alongside choices. Default: true.
params.notify: Flash taskbar and send a toast when dialog opens. Default: true.

get_user_response.desc: Poll for a pending ask_user(non_blocking=true) response. Returns PENDING until answered.

params.wait_seconds: Seconds to wait per poll. Default: 55. Max: 115.

update_dialog.desc: Send a live update into an open non-blocking ask_user dialog (macOS and Windows). Messages appear instantly in the user's browser in a scrollable "updates" panel with timestamps — no page refresh. Useful for sharing thinking state or context while waiting for the user's reply.

params.message: The message to display in the dialog

open_chat.desc: Open a persistent two-way browser chat window for extended back-and-forth conversations. Unlike ask_user (one question → one reply), this keeps the window open for multiple exchanges. Returns a chat_id. macOS and Windows only. Not supported on Linux.

params.title: Title shown in the chat window. Default: "AI Assistant"
params.subtitle: Optional subtitle (e.g. your agent or model name).

send_chat_message.desc: Send an AI message into an open chat window.

params.suggestions: Optional quick-reply suggestion chips shown to the user as tappable buttons below the message. Provide an array of short strings (e.g. ["Yes", "No", "Tell me more"]). The user can tap a chip to send it as their reply.

get_chat_messages.desc: Poll for new user messages from an open chat window. Returns PENDING or CLOSED.

params.wait_seconds: Seconds to wait per poll. Default: 55. Max: 115.

close_chat.desc: Close a chat window and free its port. Call when the session is finished.

rest.desc: Let the AI go idle and show an 'AI is resting' browser page with a wake-up button. IMPORTANT: call this tool — do NOT end the conversation or stop responding — whenever the user says 'take a rest', 'wait', 'stand by', or 'I will review': call rest(), then loop on get_user_response with the returned token until the user wakes you. macOS and Windows only. Not supported on Linux.

params.notes: Message shown to the user while resting.
params.title: Name shown in the resting UI. Default: "AI Assistant"
params.subtitle: Optional subtitle, e.g. your agent or model name.
params.timeout_seconds: Max seconds before auto-waking. Default: 3600. Max: 86400.
